questions.question: Can we read out an A/B test on any of these surfaces today?
questions.caveats: Not blocked on instrumentation: assignment and exposure both fire, and Flags Enabled moved 0 to 1 during the walk. Kept despite being marked Drop on the question list, because the Win engagement report's next move is testing hypotheses rather than mining history, and that only works if these are readable.

questions.question: Do Pro subscribers churn, and when?
questions.caveats: Answered 2026-09-16, not merely judged answerable: a cohort churn table with average days-to-churn ran in one query. No event instruments this and none should — cancellation is a Stripe state change and isPro is current state with no history, so the warehouse is the only source. 3,047 subscriptions, history to 2024-06-23, pipeline current. Two query caveats: exclude the 74 `incomplete_expired` rows (failed checkouts, never active, they inflate churn), and key churn on `status`, never on `canceled_at IS NOT NULL` — 18 active subscriptions carry a canceled_at because they are set to cancel at period end.

questions.question: How many candidates are active in a given week, and what actions does active mean?
questions.caveats: A WAU number is already circulating and is already wrong. The Active Candidates OKR anchors on `Dashboard - Candidate Dashboard Viewed`, retired in PR #732 and absent from the codebase, so the metric reads residual traffic. Re-anchoring is a PAIRED change across omni's okr: tag and gp-data-platform's semantic layer; nothing links or enforces the pairing, so the omni side is deliberately not edited alone (DATA-2173, DATA-2421, DATA-2432). Defining "active" is separate and downstream of that.

questions.question: Which Pro feature is the one people actually came for?
questions.caveats: The only fully uncovered question of the nineteen. The value-prop events carry email and the impersonation/actor fields and nothing else — no identifier for which prop or feature was shown or clicked. Needs a feature identifier on those events or a per-feature click event. Consequence worth noting: the surrounding funnel is the best instrumented in the product, so a confident conversion number is available while the "what did they want" question is unanswerable, which is a good number buying a wrong conclusion.

questions.question: Do candidates open their campaign plan, and do they read it to the end?
questions.caveats: Two things make a plan-open number a floor rather than a count. The tracker event returns early unless a generated strategy exists, so a candidate looking at an ungenerated plan fires nothing — "opened their campaign plan" means "opened a plan that exists". And the Active Candidates OKR anchored here has its own broken anchor elsewhere in this file: `Dashboard - Candidate Dashboard Viewed` was retired in PR #732 and no longer exists in the codebase. Re-anchoring spans omni and gp-data-platform's semantic layer, so it is not done here (DATA-2173, DATA-2421).

questions.question: Do candidates who abandon onboarding ever come back, or are they gone?
questions.caveats: Answerable as a query rather than by clicking, and the walk accidentally produced the exact behaviour (abandoned 18:42, resumed 20:49 across two sessions). Still needs both terms defined: what counts as abandoning, and what counts as coming back.

questions.question: Do candidates who use more of the product do better in the real outcome?
questions.caveats: Use the event, not the column: campaigns.service.ts clears Campaign.didWin when a re-running candidate moves their election date (ENG-10954), so the column is current-race-only and a multi-cycle cohort loses its history. That is the storage problem. The reason this stays caveated is selection, which no event fixes — only candidates who return after election day report an outcome, returning correlates with having won, and returning also correlates with product usage, the independent variable. The bias runs with the hypothesis, so a positive correlation is the expected result whether or not the effect is real. An external results feed joined on race id is the only fix.

surfaces.label: self_reported_outcome

questions.question: Do the AI-generated Win artifacts get opened and acted on, or just generated?
questions.caveats: Opened is covered; acted-on is covered for two of four artifacts, which corrects the walk. Campaign Story and Know Your Opponent both carry act-on events. The campaign plan itself has no copy/edit/use event, and dashboard/campaign-manager has no analytics calls at all — it is in the same investment bucket and this question cannot see it.

questions.question: How many candidates are blocked by 10DLC compliance, and how long are they stuck?
questions.caveats: "How many are blocked" is answerable from two independent signals. "How long are they stuck" is not: there is no resolution event to close the interval. 10DLC is a multi-day external process, so the duration cannot be walked — it has to come from code and data. Compliance is the hard gate on outreach, so the duration is what decides whether this is a funnel problem or a vendor problem.

questions.question: How many candidates create a voter file, across every path that creates one?
also_answers: Are people creating and downloading lists but never doing outreach on our platform?
questions.caveats: No single event answers this question as asked. `Voter Data - List Created` covers the wizard's voter-file branch only; five other paths create a real saved list and emit a different event or nothing, so a count off one event is a narrower question than the one posed (DATA-2343 sweep). Two further defects: the outreach flow may create a list on every abandoned attempt, so a raw count overstates intent (DATA-2308); and both wizard events sit behind an `isWinContextReady` gate that DROPS the event rather than misattributing it when the mode has not settled, so the wizard's own count has an unmeasured loss rate.

surfaces.label: phone_banking_call_list
surfaces.instrumented_by: Voter Outreach - Phone Banking Call List Created

questions.question: How many candidates schedule voter outreach, by channel?
also_answers: Are people creating and downloading lists but never doing outreach on our platform?
questions.caveats: BOTH OKRs anchored here are currently wrong. `Voter Outreach - Campaign Completed` stopped firing on outreach scheduling when the flow was rewritten to outreach/v2/ — it survives only on a completed door-knocking walk and on the manual self-report modal, so these metrics count door knocks and self-reports and call it outreach (DATA-2343 sweep, DATA-2432). Three of four channels have no scheduled/sent terminal at all, which reads identically to total abandonment rather than to missing instrumentation. Re-anchoring is a paired change across omni and gp-data-platform's semantic layer and is deliberately NOT done here: editing this tag alone would diverge the registry from the metric definition (DATA-2421).

questions.question: Of candidates who start an outreach flow, what share actually send, and where do the rest stop?
questions.caveats: Entry and intermediate steps fire, but the send terminal exists for robocall only. For SMS, social and phone banking the funnel has a start and no end, which reads identically to total abandonment rather than to missing instrumentation — same root cause as voter_outreach_scheduled. `Outreach - Click Create` also double-fires, so any step counted off it is inflated; that is a query-time de-duplication decision, not a gap.

questions.question: Of the people who start signup, how many complete signup, how many complete onboarding, and where do the rest stop?
questions.caveats: There is no terminal onboarding event. Completion exists only as the user property `onboardingCompleted`, so the last funnel step has to be proxied by Pledge Completed or a first-dashboard event — the DATA-2337 failure. Two further traps: signup and onboarding are separate funnels with a save point between them, so "account with no campaign" and "campaign stuck at step N" are different populations a single definition will conflate; and step events re-fire on resume, so count distinct users per step, not events.

questions.question: What do candidates do in the first week after upgrading, and does it predict whether they stay?
questions.caveats: Answerable today, both halves. First-week behaviour is a self-join on amplitude_events off the webhook-fired upgrade timestamp; retention needs Stripe subscription state, confirmed present 2026-09-16 and joinable on gp_api_db_user.meta_data.customerId. The caveat that matters: `Account - Pro Subscription Confirmed` is NOT a purchase event — it also fires on staff-granted Pro (paymentMethod 'admin') and on a degraded webhook payload, both at price 0. Comped Pro is separable on paymentMethod, never on price. Prefer the Stripe row for anything revenue-shaped.

questions.question: Which acquisition sources produce candidates who actually activate, not just sign up?
questions.caveats: Capture is in the code but has never been observed end to end: the walked signup arrived with no UTMs on the URL, so the profile carried only initial_referrer/referrer. Closing this needs one walk with UTM params present, not new instrumentation.

questions.question: How many candidates export a voter file each week, and is that growing?
also_answers: Are people creating and downloading lists but never doing outreach on our platform?
questions.caveats: Two events fire per download and they are not duplicates: `Contacts - Download` fires at click time and always fires, `Voter Data - List Exported` only from the cookie-confirmed success branch and only once the isWinContextReady and listSize gates pass. Count exports off List Exported alone; a union double-counts. The gap between the two is a free health signal (failed downloads plus the readiness race), not a demand signal.

questions.question: Of candidates who activate in a given month, how many are still active the next month, and the one after?
questions.caveats: Nothing is missing from the warehouse — every journey event lands in amplitude_events with a timestamp and a user id, and month-cohort retention off that is ordinary SQL. Blocked on TWO undefined terms: "activate" belongs to first_value_reached and "active" to weekly_active_candidates. Settle those and this closes with no code.

questions.question: What share of candidates who see the Pro value prop convert, and at which step do the rest drop?
questions.caveats: The best-instrumented flow in the product, with two reasons the number is a floor rather than exact. Both terminal events fire from the Stripe webhook inside try/catch that logs and continues, so a Segment outage loses the conversion while the upgrade succeeds, and the two can disagree because they fail independently — Stripe is the count of record. And the denominator rests on `Pro Upgrade - Banner Viewed`, seen firing on the dashboard only; if the banner renders elsewhere without firing, conversion looks better than it is. Step events also repeat on funnel re-entry, so count distinct users per step.

surfaces.label: pro_funnel_entry
surfaces.instrumented_by: Pro Upgrade - Banner: Click Get Pro

questions.question: What share of new candidates reach their first real piece of value, and how long does it take?
questions.caveats: Blocked on a definition, not on instrumentation. Timestamps and step events are sufficient; nobody has decided what "first real value" is. The proposed default is the first campaign action whose output leaves the product — every event below already fires. The same list doubles as the "active" definition weekly_active_candidates needs.
